title: The Commute (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 100bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal life philosophy absurdist Perth train commute
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The commute is the time that nobody claims belongs to them
It's between the home and work — a no-man's land of hem
You're not at home and not at work and not at liberty
The commute is scheduled to be nobody's territory

[Pre-Chorus]
I commuted for thirty years on the Fremantle line
And in that time I read a lot and stared out and did fine

[Chorus]
The commute knows something I don't know
It knows the particular rhythm of the face of those who go
The same route every morning in the same configuration
The commute is a ritual that predates the destination
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
There's a woman on my train who reads a book every single trip
She's been reading the same section for six weeks without a slip
Which suggests either the book is very good or the commute
Provides the reading and the re-reading as the route

[Bridge]
Since working from home the commute has been from bedroom to chair
Which takes eleven seconds and the birds are always there
Outside the window but there's something missing from the day
Without the commute's particular transitional display

[Outro]
Commute knows… the in-between time is the thinking time… commute knows
That's my boy
